taste_profile.design_read: Youth science short: a calm climb up one speed ladder, from walking to light, ending at a wall that never moves.
taste_profile.palette_discipline: Night ink sky, steel rail, ONE white-cyan accent for the marker; no temperature colours; red only for 'c' (the wall).
taste_profile.layout_variation: Log rail + marker, zeros counter, window plates, the LHC nines readout.
taste_profile.reference_strategy: Numbers from the brief only; AI stills as short tagged inserts.
anti_patterns: 'the falcon is the fastest animal' as fact without the dive caveat
quality_gates: Every rung's number matches the brief

typography.data: video 13's mono face (numbers, counter, readout; slashed zeros)

metadata.signature_device: One log-scale speed rail in km/h (1 to 10^9) with a single glowing marker that climbs rung by rung while a ZEROS counter ticks 0 -> 9; the top is a red 'c' line the marker approaches but never touches; streak length = log10(speed).
hero_beats: sc05 'YOU' jumps from WALK to Earth's orbit (~107,000)
sc11 the LHC nines fill while the gap under 'c' stays
metadata.honesty_grammar: MEASURED solid tab; PROBABLY outline + hatch (the falcon dive). AI: 'AI impression' on S1-S3. Drawings: 'drawn · not to scale' (orbit inset, energy curve). The rail is labelled 'km/h · log scale'. Numbers on rungs are the brief's values; '~' where the brief gives a range.

pages.page: You walk at about five kilometres
an hour. A cheetah sprints at
about a hundred.
A diving falcon hits nearly four
hundred.
Sound outruns them all at over
twelve hundred. But sitting still,
you're doing over a hundred thousand,
riding Earth around the Sun.
The fastest thing we've ever built,
the Parker Solar Probe,
reached nearly seven hundred thousand,
falling toward the Sun.
Light does over a billion.
And nothing with mass can catch
it: the closer you get,
the more energy each step costs,
without end.
The Large Hadron Collider pushes protons
to within a hair of light
speed. Close. But never all the
way.

music.prompt: Instrumental bed for a curious, uplifting science short about speed, from walking pace to the speed of light, 58 seconds, about 100 BPM, D major. A light, steady texture from the very first beat: soft synth pulse, plucked strings and a gentle shimmering pad. Keep the same instruments, density and loudness from 0 to about 52 seconds: no intro build, no drop, no breakdown, no hits, no risers, no fade, no silence, no drums. Then in the last 6 seconds play one clear resolved final cadence (IV - V - I) and end on a single sustained major chord that rings out naturally for about 3 seconds.
